terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Plaut. Cas. 3.4.3: ad tē hercle ībam commodum, I was just coming to you (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With a pluperfect and cum it is “had just … when …” (Cic. Att. 13.9.1; Ter. Eun. 2.3.52, Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short: colloquial, and in post-classical prose.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.23.1: tantum quod ex Arpīnātī vēneram, cum mihi ā tē litterae redditae sunt (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: modo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 87–88.
Lewis & Short: commodum · Lewis & Short: tantum. Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-terentius), checked against the editions named there.

phrases.english: When? — Today. — How long ago? — Just now.
